name: Burhān al-Dīn Abū al-Fatḥ Nāṣir ibn ʿAbd al-Sayyid al-Muṭarrizī
summary: Khwārazmian grammarian and Ḥanafī jurist, called the successor of al-Zamakhsharī, whose short al-Miṣbāḥ fī al-naḥw was a first book of grammar in the madrasas of the East.
bio: Al-Muṭarrizī was born in Khwārazm in 538/1144, the year al-Zamakhsharī died, and was later called his successor (khalīfa), since he followed him in grammar and in Muʿtazilī theology. He was a Ḥanafī jurist, and his al-Mughrib explains the rare words of the Ḥanafī law books.

His al-Miṣbāḥ fī al-naḥw sets out the essentials of grammar in five short chapters and was a reading book in the madrasas of Iran, Central Asia, India and the Ottoman lands; it was printed with al-ʿAwāmil and other primers. He also commented on al-Ḥarīrī's Maqāmāt. He died in Khwārazm in 610/1213.
